name: Interconnected Map Graph
description: The world as a data structure: rooms as nodes, connections as edges, and edges optionally gated by powers, so the whole lock-and-key topology of a metroidvania lives in one queryable place. It owns the graph, the player's current room, first-visit facts, and region grouping — the things every other system argues about when they each keep their own copy. It deliberately does not render anything: ui.map_reveal_system decides what the player is allowed to see, and ui.minimap draws it. It also does not evaluate gates; world.ability_gate owns pass/reject, and this component only consumes the outcome to update which edges are currently traversable. The payoff is the query layer: reachable-from-here given current powers is a graph traversal over owned data, which is what backtrack hints, sequence-break detection, and completion tracking all actually need.

inputs.name: rooms
inputs.description: Room records: id, bounds, region. Bounds place the graph over the level so crossing a room boundary can be detected from position alone.

inputs.name: connections
inputs.description: Edges between rooms, each optionally naming a gate id. A connection that names a gate is locked topology; one that does not is open from the start.

inputs.name: startRoomId
inputs.description: Where the player begins. Also the root for reachability queries before any powers are acquired — the measure of what the 'empty' player can already do.

inputs.name: regionKey
inputs.description: Which room field groups rooms into regions. Regions are the unit of map coloring and 'region unlocked' announcements, not of traversal.

outputs.name: unlockedRegionIds
outputs.description: Regions with at least one visited room — the coarse progress signal a world map colors in.
